slides.title: Bias Distorts Insight Without Any Dishonesty
bullets: Field-generated insight is vulnerable to well-documented cognitive biases
An unaware MSL will quietly distort the picture over time
This happens through normal information processing, not bad intent

slides.title: Confirmation Bias Weights What You Already Believe
bullets: Tendency to notice and remember what confirms existing beliefs
Contradicting information gets discounted or simply not registered
An MSL may recall supportive conversations more readily than complicating ones

slides.title: Seek Out What Might Prove You Wrong
bullets: Deliberately seek disconfirming perspectives, not just corroborating ones
Practise active reflexivity — ask what assumption is shaping this reading
Drawn from qualitative research methodology literature

slides.title: Selection Bias Skews Who Gets Heard
bullets: Engagement naturally concentrates on the most accessible, enthusiastic experts
That skews the resulting picture of what physicians think
Can miss the harder-to-reach perspectives with the most important insight

slides.title: Deliberately Widen Who You Engage
bullets: Include a broader, more representative range of physicians
Not only the easiest or most favourably disposed ones
Connects to the territory and segmentation discipline from Module 3

slides.title: One Vivid Conversation Can Outweigh a Real Pattern
bullets: A recent, memorable conversation can feel more significant than it is
It can get reported with more weight than a quieter, broader pattern
Reviewing insight logs over a longer window corrects for this

slides.title: Build Bias-Checking Into Routine Practice
bullets: State the evidentiary basis explicitly in every written insight
Periodically review your own log for one-sided reporting
Seek a colleague's perspective on ambiguous or high-stakes insights

takeaway.title: Confirmation, selection and recency bias quietly distort field insight if unchecked
bullets: Seek disconfirming views and a wider range of physicians, not just easy ones
Review your insight log over time, not just the latest visit
State your evidence honestly and triangulate high-stakes insights with colleagues
